parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This is a presentation-layer file, and it contains a business rule. In `LoanController.lend`, the check `if (body.days < 1 || body.days > 60)` throws `LendingError('INVALID', 'A loan lasts between 1 and 60 days')`. That limit is a domain invariant about how long a loan may last, so the domain layer should own it. The flag about the shared literal 60 supports this: `src/business/model/Loan.ts:3` uses the same number, so the business layer already appears to model the limit. The controller copies it instead of leaving it to the domain.

The rest of the controller fits its role. The injected `LendingService` and `LoanHistoryService` come from the business layer, which presentation may depend on, so they are normal dependency wiring. The `LendRequest` and `ReturnRequest` DTOs, the `HttpResult` return values with status codes, and the `renderLoan` view calls are all presentation concerns. `giveBack` and `historyOf` only pass calls through to the services. The flags about controller logic density are confirmed, and the violation they point to is this duration check.
